subtopics.name: Discharge planning and continuity of care

questions.stem: The nurse on a labor and delivery unit receives report. Which client should the nurse see first?

options.text: A client at 39 weeks, 4 cm dilated, requesting an epidural
A client at 32 weeks with sudden severe abdominal pain, a rigid uterus and dark vaginal bleeding
A client 1 hour after birth who wants to breastfeed
A client at 38 weeks whose membranes ruptured with clear fluid and a reassuring fetal heart rate

rationale.correct: Placental abruption threatens both lives and needs immediate action.

perOption.a: Needs attention soon but is stable.
perOption.b: Suggests placental abruption, an emergency for the client and fetus.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Maternal-newborn nursing texts (e.g. Perry; Lowdermilk)

questions.stem: On a postpartum unit, for each task, indicate the most appropriate staff member.

rows.text: First assessment of a client transferred from labor and delivery
Giving scheduled oral ibuprofen to a stable client
Helping a stable client to the bathroom for the first time after birth

rationale.correct: Match tasks to scope and stability.

perOption.r1:c1: Initial assessment is an RN responsibility.
perOption.r2:c2: Within LPN scope for a stable client.
perOption.r3:c1: First ambulation after birth needs RN assessment because of fainting and bleeding risk.
perOption.r3:c2: The RN should assess the first time.
perOption.r3:c3: Later ambulation can be delegated once the client is stable.

questions.stem: On a pediatric unit, which child should the nurse see first?

options.text: A 3-year-old with a cast who is crying for a parent
A 6-month-old with bronchiolitis whose respiratory rate rose from 48 to 72/min with nasal flaring
A 10-year-old with diabetes asking for a snack before gym
A 14-year-old after appendectomy with pain 3/10

rationale.correct: Infants decompensate quickly; respiratory distress comes first.

perOption.a: Emotional need; can be addressed after urgent problems.
perOption.b: Increasing work of breathing in an infant can lead quickly to respiratory failure.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment

Coordinate with the social worker for housing and schedule outpatient follow-up before discharge

rationale.correct: Discharge planning addresses social needs and follow-up.

perOption.b: Transition planning reduces relapse and readmission.

questions.stem: A client with a new diagnosis of heart failure is going home. Which items belong in the discharge plan? Select all that apply.

options.text: A follow-up appointment within 7 days
Daily weight monitoring with clear instructions on when to call
A reconciled medication list
Instructions to stop all medications if feeling well
Referral to cardiac rehabilitation or home health as needed
A high-sodium diet to keep blood pressure up

rationale.correct: Discharge plans include follow-up, monitoring, medications and referrals.

perOption.b: Weight gain is an early sign of fluid overload.
perOption.f: Sodium is limited in heart failure.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
